sources.publication_and_underlying_material_iden: The actual original names J. C. Escher as main compiler, N. Henriksen as project coordinator, Bengaard and Henriksen for North and East Greenland onshore compilation, and Pulvertaft for offshore compilation. Greenland onshore geology uses published and unpublished GGU maps. Topography is compiled and reproduced by KMS and GGU from their published and unpublished topographic maps for land and the Inland Ice margin. Ice-surface contours use GEOSAT and ERS-1 altimetry, compiled/modelled by S. Ekholm of KMS; sub-ice bedrock contours use airborne radar ice-thickness data and KMS modelling. The imprint specifies WGS84, UTM zone24 and 1995 printing. This positively identified GGU national geological/topographic compilation is not a copy of the held USGS PP1386-C glacier atlas or the separately held 1997 GEUS Dove Bugt sheet. No independence of every shared older control datum is claimed; the original identifies the actual compilation project and source families.

sources.limits: Not a river register or continuous natural-watercourse survey. correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern opening on the western volcanic apron of the Payún Matru field
correspondence.finding: The selected opening occupies a dry, locally incised volcanic apron. Small runnels and sediment-filled hollows lead southwest toward the western margin corridor. This is ordinary terrain and drainage-corridor correspondence; no river label or perennial-flow claim is supplied.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward western lava-margin corridor
correspondence.finding: The selection follows a broad southward corridor along and locally across the margin of dark rough lava terrain. Adjacent sediment-covered ground and minor runnels form the receiving setting. The source supports that ordinary corridor, without turning lava-surface texture into a named river or claiming an exact wet channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeast-trending apron and broad middle turn
correspondence.finding: The route continues southeast along the volcanic-foot plain, then makes a broad southward and northeastward turn around rougher intervening relief into the middle sediment-filled floor. The overlapping original views expose the transition and its small converging dry runnels at ordinary valley/fan scale. No separately named tributary is established.

correspondence.component_scope: East- and southeast-trending middle embayment
correspondence.finding: The selected middle corridor occupies a sediment-filled embayment among rough lava surfaces and eroded low relief, broadening eastward. Its dry floor, pale patches and small joining runnels are visible in the original. No lake outlet, glacier transfer or managed passage is evidenced here. This completed bounded geography does not establish a single named natural river.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower fan/plain continuation through the eastern volcanic-depression terrain to the coincident stored source and render endings
correspondence.finding: The previously read complete overview includes the lower volcanic plain, pale local depressions and rough lava surfaces through the eastern selected ending. It provides regional terrain coverage, but does not sufficiently establish the entire selected receiving continuation from the lower fan/plain through that terrain to the final ending. The attempted closer terminal view has no verified terminal result and is wholly excluded. This is one bounded lower receiving-link gap, not a requirement to trace exact banks or a currently wet thread, and not a finding that no drainage exists. No nearby pale playa is substituted for the selected ending.

correspondence.component_scope: northern opening and westward nunatak passage
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening and short westward/southwestward parts lie among small exposed-bedrock islands and intervening ice terrain. The initial westward bend and the subsequent southward interval are visible on the original. No named natural-watercourse trace is established.

correspondence.component_scope: western southward turn and eastern return
correspondence.finding: The long western/southward part skirts and crosses generalized rock/ice margins, turns east between elongated exposed-rock ridges, then bends southeast and south into the broader pale ice corridor. All intermediate stored joins are accounted for at the map scale. Blue ice-contour linework is not treated as a river.

correspondence.component_scope: middle ice and rock island corridor
correspondence.finding: The selection continues east and southeast through the broad corridor between elongated rock ridges to the southwest and smaller rock islands to the east. Its short joins and bends pass the eastern ends of mapped ridges and continue toward the denser coastal bedrock belt. These are ordinary terrain observations, not proof of glacier hydraulic routing.

correspondence.component_scope: lower exposed rock and margin passages
correspondence.finding: The lower eastward then southeastward selection traverses the more closely spaced coastal rock/ice-margin mosaic. The enlarged original exposes the crossing of a broad mapped rock mass, intervening pale passages and the next southeastern rock-margin approach. No distinct selected lake or missing lake-to-feeder transfer is identified in the original.

correspondence.component_scope: coastal approach and separate terminal settings
correspondence.finding: The final eastward parts and short northward ending occupy the coastal bedrock/ice-margin belt beside small unnamed embayments north of the directly printed Tasiilap Karra / Kap Gustav Holm cape label. The source and rendered endings were considered separately and both fall within this same ordinary coastal-margin setting; the rendered position is slightly northward of the source position. The national map does not justify exact present land/ice/water assignment or an ordinary river-mouth claim.

correspondence.component_scope: northwestern mountain opening
correspondence.finding: The chosen northwestern opening and first short eastward parts lie in the mapped mountain ice/exposed-rock mosaic immediately east of the wider Gunnbjørn Fjeld and Watkins Bjerge labels. The opening bends and initial narrow ice/rock passage are all exposed in the original. The mountain names are regional references, not river or glacier assignments.

correspondence.component_scope: eastward upper ridge and ice margin
correspondence.finding: The selected path follows a generally eastward upper passage, traverses a generalized exposed-rock ridge/mass and its ice margin, and turns southeast then south at the eastern end of that mass. All intervening short parts and joins are covered. The original does not map this whole itinerary as one named natural river.

correspondence.component_scope: middle southward ice trough
correspondence.finding: The middle southward and southeastward sequence occupies the broad ice passage between long exposed-rock ridges and isolated rock masses. It passes the western side of a long north-south rock ridge, continues between the next flanking massifs and enters the lower straight southward corridor. No contemporary route over or beneath the ice is inferred from the selected line or blue topographic contours.

correspondence.component_scope: lower ice trough and coastal rock margin
correspondence.finding: The selected line continues down the pale ice corridor between the western and eastern bedrock ridges, then bends southeast through the lower margin beside the coastal exposed-rock belt. The original supplies continuous ordinary geographic context through all these bends and joins. No distinct selected lake passage or missing basin transfer is required or claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: coastal approach and separate source render endings
correspondence.finding: The last southeastward parts reach a small coastal opening between mapped rock promontories west of the Kap Ravn reference. The source endpoint is the more landward/northwestern terminal position, while the rendered endpoint extends farther southeast toward the coast in the same ordinary terminal setting. Both were considered separately on the original. The nearby larger Nansen Fjord lies to the southwest and is not substituted for this selected opening. National-scale historical mapping does not establish a precise present river mouth, current glacier front or exact terminal land/ice/water class.

correspondence.component_scope: eastern opening and polvorillas reach
correspondence.finding: The selected eastern opening descends south through a confined tributary valley and successive side-gully joins. Ojinaga’s Relieve plate directly labels this eastern drainage Polvorillas. The opening is treated as the chosen model start, not a verified named spring or an independently surveyed headwater.

correspondence.component_scope: southwestern descent and southern turn
correspondence.finding: The eastern drainage continues southwest and rounds the southern bend into a broader receiving valley. Ojinaga covers the eastern approach; the adjoining northern Camargo plate shows the connecting wash at the bend and its meeting with the northward valley. The name is bounded to the mapped eastern reach, without inventing a precise name-change point.

correspondence.component_scope: northern camargo middle valley
correspondence.finding: The route follows the connected wash northwest and north along the northern Camargo tongue, beside Sierra Mojina. The readable original shows the same receiving valley, tributary joins and continuation across the municipal clipping boundary. A separate name for this middle interval is not established.

correspondence.component_scope: la copa receiving approach
correspondence.finding: The northward middle valley passes into Ojinaga and bends northwest onto the drainage directly labeled La Copa. Several east-side tributaries enter the same lower corridor. The map supplies a receiving-watercourse identity rather than a claim that every upper branch carries this name.

correspondence.component_scope: la copa northwestern reach
correspondence.finding: The selected course continues west and northwest across the broad alluvial floor southwest of Sierra El Guaje. La Copa is printed on this connected lower drainage, distinct from the eastern Polvorillas label and the separately mapped Alamitos drainage farther north.

correspondence.component_scope: lower plain and aldama approach
correspondence.finding: The lower corridor trends northwest through the plain toward the Ojinaga–Aldama map boundary. The adjoining thematic plates show compatible receiving-floor and drainage continuity. Generalized map correspondence is sufficient here; no present wet thread or exact bank alignment is required.

correspondence.component_scope: final bend and interior draining floor
correspondence.finding: The final selected parts turn west and southwest within the mapped interior alluvial drainage floor east of Sierra El Jabalí. Aldama’s enlarged southeastern map shows the relevant drainage branches and the complete endpoint setting. No terminal lake name, surveyed closed-basin boundary or independently named downstream watercourse is established.
